slot.brief: Ask how the speed of sound in an ideal gas changes when pressure is doubled at constant temperature / when temperature is raised; pick the correct qualitative option.

stem: For a given ideal gas, its absolute temperature is raised from $T$ to $4T$. Assuming the ratio of specific heats remains constant, the speed of sound changes by a factor of:

verdicts.working: For an ideal gas, speed of sound is proportional to √T when γ is constant. Raising T to 4T doubles the speed.

working:
$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma R T}{M}}$; hence $\dfrac{v_2}{v_1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{4T}{T}} = 2$.

Independent check: For an ideal gas, speed of sound is proportional to √T when γ is constant. Raising T to 4T doubles the speed.
